description.summary: darken every output but one (cinema mode)

protocol.description:
Lets a client switch the desktop into a "cinema mode": one output stays as it is and every other output goes dark, so a film on the lit output isn't competing with a bright second monitor. Optionally the dark outputs glow faintly in the colors found along the border of the lit output, as if its light spilled over onto the screens around it.
Like the display filter, this is a pure mechanism: the compositor only applies what was asked for, and *when* cinema mode should be on is the client's business. Nothing here needs the user's permission, since the effect is purely visual, never hides anything the user can't bring back by switching it off, and ends by itself if the client does.
The mode is tied to the lifetime of the object: when a client destroys it or disconnects (including by crashing), whatever it requested is withdrawn, so a dead shell can never leave screens black. If several live objects have made requests, the most recent request wins as a whole (the output and the glow of the object that made it). When the object that made the most recent request goes away, the most recent request of the remaining live objects takes over. Binding the global or creating an object requests nothing by itself.
Dark outputs keep showing the pointer, and input keeps working on them; only their picture is replaced. The compositor fades the dark outputs in and out over a fraction of a second, so the client doesn't need to animate anything.
If the lit output is unplugged while the mode is on, the mode does nothing until an output of that name is back (rather than blacking out every screen).

request.name: destroy
request.description: Ends whatever this object requested; the outputs fade back in unless another live object still has cinema mode switched on.

request.name: enable
request.description:
Turns cinema mode on with `output` as the one that stays lit; every other output goes dark. If `output` is null the compositor picks the output the user is working on at the moment of the request: the one with the keyboard-focused window, otherwise the one under the pointer. The pick is made once; it doesn't follow the pointer or focus afterwards.
Sending enable again, with the same or another output, keeps the mode on and moves the lit screen (the dark ones fade as needed). The glow strength set with set_glow is kept.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output that stays lit, or null for the current one

request.name: disable
request.description: Turns cinema mode off: the dark outputs fade back to normal. The glow strength set with set_glow is kept for the next enable.

request.name: set_glow

description.summary: set the strength of the glow on the dark outputs

request.description:
Sets how strongly the dark outputs pick up the colors along the border of the lit output: 0 turns the glow off (the dark outputs stay plain black, the default), 100 is the strongest. Values above 100 are treated as 100. A stronger glow is both brighter and reaches further across the dark outputs.
The glow follows the picture on the lit output as it changes. It only shows on dark outputs, and only while cinema mode is on; the value is remembered either way. Takes effect at once, also while cinema mode is already on.
